## F06.input-contract — Input contract

Definition: What a hook receives: fields, format, channel.
- claude-code [supported, unverified] When an event fires and a matcher matches, Claude Code passes JSON context about the event to the hook: for command hooks on stdin, for HTTP hooks as the POST request body. All hook inputs share `session_id`, `cwd`, and `hook_event_name`. Hook input also carries `prompt_id`, a UUID for the current user prompt (requires Claude Code v2.1.196 or later). | ev: E-claude-code-09907, E-claude-code-00354, E-claude-code-01230
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Every command hook receives one JSON object on stdin. Fields include session_id (the current Codex session id; subagent hooks use the parent session id) and transcript_path (a path to the session transcript file, if any). ## F06.output-blocking — Output and blocking semantics

Definition: Exit codes or JSON that allow, deny, ask or modify.
- claude-code [partial, verified] A `PreToolUse` hook runs before the rest of the permission flow and can allow, deny, or modify requests; if it rejects a tool call, the call doesn't execute and Claude receives the rejection message. A `TeammateIdle` hook exits with code 2 to send feedback and keep the teammate working. | limit: A hook that returns `allow` does not skip the deny and ask rules; a `PreToolUse` hook allow also can't approve an `rm` or `rmdir` removal targeting a critical path. | ev: E-claude-code-01463, E-claude-code-00434, E-claude-code-00271, E-claude-code-01524
- codex-cli [partial, verified] A PreToolUse hook can block or rewrite a tool call and inspect its JSON arguments. A hook that exits 0 with no output is treated as success and Codex continues. | limit: An explicit supported denial can block an action, but a PreToolUse callback error, timeout, or malformed response can fail the hook without blocking the tool. Hooks are a useful guardrail, not a complete enforcement boundary. | ev: E-codex-cli-01775, E-codex-cli-01830, E-codex-cli-01259, E-codex-cli-01782
- copilot-cli [supported, unverified] A preToolUse hook can allow execution (by doing nothing) or deny it (by returning a structured response), and can approve or deny tool executions. Hook JSON output must be on a single line to be valid. Hooks run synchronously and block agent execution. | ev: E-copilot-cli-01406, E-copilot-cli-01939, E-copilot-cli-02584, E-copilot-cli-01951
- copilot-vscode [supported, unverified] A `PreToolUse` hook runs before the agent invokes a tool and can block an operation, request approval, or change tool input. To block a terminal tool call in the Local harness, use a Preview `PreToolUse` hook that returns `permissionDecision: "deny"`. When several hooks target one event, all run, and for `PreToolUse` `deny` overrides `ask`, which overrides `allow`. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00157, E-copilot-vscode-00924, E-copilot-vscode-01496
- cursor [supported, verified] Exit code 0 means the hook succeeded and its JSON output is used; exit code 2 blocks the action, equivalent to returning permission: deny. For permission hooks, invalid JSON or a response that does not match the hook's schema blocks the action. The nested permissionDecision and updatedInput map to permission and updated_input. failClosed can be set for critical hooks. | ev: E-cursor-00816, E-cursor-00817, E-cursor-01077, E-cursor-00786
- gemini-cli [partial, verified] Under the exit-code guidance, a blocking exit blocks the tool for Tool events (the agent continues) and aborts the turn for Agent/Model events. BeforeModel's Exit Code 2 (Block Turn) aborts the turn and skips the LLM call. | limit: BeforeToolSelection: Limitations: Does not support `decision`, `continue`, or (the rest of the field list is cut off in the quote). | ev: E-gemini-cli-01901, E-gemini-cli-01900, E-gemini-cli-00454, E-gemini-cli-00456
- grok-build [partial, verified] Exit code 0 allows, exit code 2 denies; only an explicit `deny` blocks. For passive events, stdout is ignored; exit 0 on success. | limit: `PreToolUse` is the only blocking event. Everything else, including timeouts, crashes and malformed output, is fail-open: the failure is recorded in the session but the tool call proceeds. | ev: E-grok-build-00261, E-grok-build-00257

## F06.matchers — Matcher semantics

Definition: How a hook selects the tool or event it fires on.
- claude-code [supported, verified] The `matcher` field matches a different value depending on the hook event: tool-based hooks match the tool name, while `Notification` hooks match the notification type. Use a single string with `|` to match multiple tools (for example `Edit|Write`); a JSON array means the hook never fires. An empty `matcher` on a Notification hook fires on all notification types. | ev: E-claude-code-00349, E-claude-code-07614, E-claude-code-09711
- codex-cli [partial, verified] The matcher field is a regex string that filters when hooks fire. Matcher groups are set per hook event (such as PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, SessionStart). PermissionRequest filters on tool name; support includes Bash, apply_patch, and MCP tool names. | limit: Only some current Codex events honor matcher. | ev: E-codex-cli-01766, E-codex-cli-00913, E-codex-cli-01768, E-codex-cli-01769
- copilot-cli [undocumented, verified] swept for: matcher; hooks?\b.{0,40}(match|filter|tool name|pattern); hits 2, reviewed 2; positive control `copilot`: 4865 hits
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] For Claude-format hook files, which require `chat.useClaudeHooks`, Local parses nested commands but ignores matcher values, so every command for the event runs. To filter Local hook behavior, check the event input inside the hook script. | limit: The Local harness parses the `matcher` field for compatibility with Claude Code, but ignores matcher values. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-00153, E-copilot-vscode-01491, E-copilot-vscode-02281
- cursor [supported, unverified] A matcher is a regex string that filters when a hook runs; an empty string or * matches everything. For beforeShellExecution it runs against the shell command string; for preToolUse / postToolUse / postToolUseFailure it filters by tool type (values include Shell, Read, Write, Grep, Delete, Task, and MCP:‹tool_name›); for subagentStart it runs against the subagent type. | ev: E-cursor-00843, E-cursor-00846, E-cursor-00847, E-cursor-00845
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] The `matcher` field is a regex (for tools) or exact string (for lifecycle) that filters when the hook runs; `"*"` or `""` matches all occurrences. Any built-in tool (for example `read_file`) can be matched, and MCP-server tools follow a documented naming pattern. | ev: E-gemini-cli-01851, E-gemini-cli-01820, E-gemini-cli-01859, E-gemini-cli-01860
- grok-build [supported, verified] `matcher` is a regular expression tested against the tool name (Claude tool names such as `Bash`, `Read`, and `Edit` are mapped to Grok's automatically); omit it to match everything. | ev: E-grok-build-00254

## F06.trust-enable — Trust and enable controls

Definition: How hooks are trusted, reviewed, disabled or locked by policy.
- claude-code [partial, verified] An admin can restrict which hooks run and restrict HTTP hook URLs (allowManagedHooksOnly). Hooks in managed settings run shell commands, so interactive users see a security approval dialog before Claude Code applies them. Passing --settings with disableAllHooks set to true turns hooks off for that run. | limit: Without --bare, a -p session runs the hooks in a project's .claude/settings.json, even in a folder you've never trusted, and shows no workspace trust dialog. | ev: E-claude-code-00131, E-claude-code-13381, E-claude-code-12239, E-claude-code-09695
- codex-cli [supported, verified] Non-managed hooks must be reviewed and trusted before they run, and plugin hooks must likewise be reviewed and trusted. /hooks lets you inspect configured hooks, trust new or changed hooks, or disable non-managed hooks before they run. Codex ignores project-local hooks when the project is untrusted. | ev: E-codex-cli-03965, E-codex-cli-01175, E-codex-cli-02966, E-codex-cli-04207
- copilot-cli [supported, verified] A user setting can disable all hooks, both repository-level and user-level. Repository hooks load in prompt mode (-p) when GITHUB_COPILOT_PROMPT_MODE_REPO_HOOKS is set to true, and also load automatically when the folder is already trusted or COPILOT_ALLOW_ALL is set. Hook configuration changes are loaded when the CLI starts. | ev: E-copilot-cli-03748, E-copilot-cli-03584, E-copilot-cli-02580
- copilot-vscode [partial, verified] Setting the `ChatHooks` policy to `false` makes the Local harness ignore hook configurations and not execute hook commands. Workspace hook files are subject to Workspace Trust. With managed `allowManagedHooksOnly: true`, plugin hooks run only when the plugin is force-enabled by a managed `enabledPlugins` entry; user enablement alone is not sufficient. | limit: The `ChatHooks` setting 'is only used by the Local agent harness'; the policy disables hooks 'in the Local harness'. | ev: E-copilot-vscode-02822, E-copilot-vscode-01187, E-copilot-vscode-00150, E-copilot-vscode-01486
- cursor [supported, verified] Project hooks load and run automatically when team members open the project in a trusted workspace, and the workspace must be trusted to run them. Claude Code hooks load when the Third-Party Imports setting is enabled (on by default). A Hooks tab in Customize and a Hooks output channel show configured and executed hooks and errors. | ev: E-cursor-03110, E-cursor-03111, E-cursor-01072, E-cursor-03123
- gemini-cli [supported, unverified] hooksConfig.enabled is the canonical toggle for the hooks system; when disabled, no hooks are executed (default true). Project hooks (./.gemini/...) are untrusted by default. Gemini CLI fingerprints project hooks (quote truncated after 'If a hook's name or command changes'). The /hooks command can disable a hook by name. | ev: E-gemini-cli-00342, E-gemini-cli-01908, E-gemini-cli-01832, E-gemini-cli-00561
- grok-build [supported, verified] Project hooks require trust before they run: the first time you open a repo with hooks, grant it with `/hooks-trust` or by launching with `--trust`.
